item.title: Quantized integral models of reductive monoids
item.description: arXiv:2610.21193v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct quantized integral models of reductive monoids and establish their finite-generation properties. We also describe the quantized coordinate rings of the basic affine spaces explicitly in terms of Lusztig's dual canonical bases. The results will be used in the companion paper \cite{CJ2} to establish a classification theorem for split reductive monoids over arbitrary connected base schemes.
item.dc:creator: Jingren Chi, Simon Jacques

item.title: Continuous representations of the meta Hahn algebra and special functions
item.description: arXiv:2610.21494v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Infinite families of biorthogonal rational functions are constructed using infinite dimensional representations of the three-generated meta Hahn algebra. Continuous Hahn and continuous dual Hahn polynomials are also recovered along the way using an embedding of the Hahn algebra inside the meta Hahn. Rational functions and polynomials arise as transition coefficients between eigenvectors and generalized eigenvectors, and their algebraic properties follow naturally from the relations of the meta Hahn algebra. Finally, biorthogonality relations are established for the rational functions introduced in the paper.
item.dc:creator: Quentin Labriet, Luc Vinet

item.title: A Krause-type recollement for Q-shaped derived categories
item.description: arXiv:2610.21507v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let k be a commutative noetherian hereditary ring and let Q be a small, Hom-finite, locally bounded k-linear category admitting a Serre functor and satisfying the strong retraction property, with nilpotent pseudo-radical. For every k-algebra A, we construct a recollement of the Q-shaped homo?topy category KQ(A Inj) of objectwise injective Q-shaped modules by its full subcategory Kac Q (A Inj) of exact objects and the Q-shaped derived category DQ(A). The construction uses complete hereditary cotorsion pairs and does not require A to be noetherian. If A is left noetherian, both KQ(A Inj) and Kac Q (A Inj) are compactly generated by special preenvelopes of finitely generat?ed stalk modules. We identify (Kac Q (A Inj))c with the idempotent completion of (KQ(A Inj))c/LI ((DQ(A))c ), where LI is the fully faithful left adjoint of the localization. This paper builds on and generalizes works of Krause and Liu
item.dc:creator: Yajun Ma, Peiru Yang

item.title: A Proof of the Jung-Kim Conjecture on the Centers of Walled Brauer Algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.21576v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a unified account of the five families of Khovanov arc algebras $K_n^m$, $K_n^{-\infty}$, $K_n^{+\infty}$, $K_n^\infty$ and $K_\infty^\infty$ in the framework of level-two tensor product categorifications, making explicit a perspective familiar to specialists. Our main application is a proof of the Jung--Kim conjecture: over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, the centre of every walled Brauer algebra is generated by supersymmetric polynomials in its Jucys--Murphy elements. We also give a homogeneous basis of the centre in terms of arc diagrams, for the grading induced by $K_\infty^\infty$. The proof combines a calculation of the arc-algebra centre with an explicit comparison of central actions under the Brundan--Stroppel Morita equivalence and Brundan-Kleshchev isomorphism. Along the way, we explain the relation between $K_n^{-\infty}$ and classical super duality, and identify $K_n^{-\infty}$ and $K_n^{+\infty}$ as Ringel duals. We also revisit mixed Schur--Weyl duality for general linear Lie superalgebras within the same framework.
item.dc:creator: Shunsuke Hirota

item.title: Generalized Cluster Algebra Homomorphisms Induced by Cluster Tube Embeddings
item.description: arXiv:2610.21822v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We relate multiplication formulas for regular modules in coefficient-free acyclic affine cluster algebras with skew-symmetric exchange matrices to the imaginary exchange relations of Reading-Stella. Introducing a parameter $z$ into the construction of Zhou-Zhu, we define a weighted cluster character on cluster tubes that satisfies generalized exchange relations of type $C_{n-1}$ and yields a bijection between indecomposable rigid objects and cluster variables. Using the multiplication formulas and difference property of Ding-Xiao-Xu, we show that non-homogeneous tube embeddings induce injective homomorphisms into ordinary affine cluster algebras under $z\mapsto X_\delta$. Comparison with Reading-Stella's relations identifies $X_\delta$ with the corresponding theta function, giving a representation-theoretic interpretation of the generalized exchange parameter.
item.dc:creator: Mingze Li

item.title: Modules and operator rings of Reynolds algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.21829v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a module theory for weighted Reynolds algebras by constructing an associa?tive ring that records the algebra action and the module operator. The categories of left and right Reynolds modules are equivalent to the corresponding module categories over this ring, and their tensor products agree under these equivalences. We construct free Reynolds modules and give an explicit graded description of the operator ring for idempotent classical Reynolds operators fixing the identity. When the Reynolds operator on the algebra is bijective, modules with bijective module operators correspond to differential modules satisfying an invertibility condition. The operator ring transfers the Hom-tensor adjunction, Morita theory and derived functors to Reynolds modules. Explicit computations over a field show that the identity operator gives an operator ring of global dimension one, whereas the zero operator gives one of infinite global dimension.
item.dc:creator: Jun He, Xiao-Song Peng, Chenghao Zhang, Yi Zhang

item.title: Weight structures and t-structures on the triangulated category generated by a $\mathbb{P}$-object
item.description: arXiv:2610.21859v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: $\mathbb{P}$-objects were introduced by Huybrechts and Thomas as a generalization of spherical objects. We classify the weight structures and t-structures on the triangulated category generated by a $\mathbb{P}^n[k]$-object in the sense of Krug. For $n=1$, this recovers the classification of weight structures and t-structures on the triangulated category generated by a spherical object due to Holm, Jorgensen and Yang. We also compute the Koszul-dual model of the triangulated category generated by a $\mathbb{P}^n[k]$-object.
item.dc:creator: Lukas Bonfert

item.title: Double affine Frobenius Hecke algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.22156v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We define double affine Hecke algebras associated to the $\textrm{GL}_n$ and $\textrm{SL}_n$ root data, decorated by a supersymmetric Frobenius superalgebra. When the Frobenius algebra is the group algebra of a finite group, we obtain new double affine versions of the quantum wreath Hecke algebras, and in particular of the affine Yokonuma-Hecke algebras. We prove a basis theorem, describe the centre for generic parameters, and define polynomial representations. We also provide a diagrammatic interpretation, from which we deduce certain involutions and symmetries of the algebra, and use it to describe an $\textrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$-action by outer automorphisms.
item.dc:creator: Niccol\`o Mattarei

item.title: Double covers of tori for p=2 and genuine functions
item.description: arXiv:2610.22171v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In his work on $L$-embeddings and double covers of tori over local fields, Kaletha associates to a maximal torus $S$ in a connected reductive group a canonical double cover $S(F)_{\pm}$ and introduces a genuine sign function $a_S$ associated to a genuine character of $S(F)_{\pm}$. We give two constructions of this genuine sign function over a non-archimedean local field, including residual characteristic $2$. The first uses rootwise lifts to the double cover; the second, in characteristic zero, uses the exponential map. Under explicit ramification conditions, both constructions yield genuine sign functions which, in odd residual characteristic, agree with his construction. We also illustrate the case of $\mathrm{PGL}_2$. A brief announcement of the first construction appears in Appendix D of that work.
item.dc:creator: L\'eo Gratien, Nhat Hoang Le, Kazuki Tokimoto

item.title: Rectangular Symmetry for Catalan Functions
item.description: arXiv:2610.21535v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Katabolizable tableaux provide a combinatorial formula for the Schur coefficients of Catalan functions. We prove that a tableau involution preserves katabolizability under antidiagonal reflection of any upper root ideal. This involution complements shape and content in a fixed rectangle and preserves charge. We obtain a bijective proof of the rectangular symmetry of these coefficients.
item.dc:creator: Hyeonjae Choi

item.title: A family of algebras that connects positroids, the Theta conjecture, the Delta conjecture, and Eulerian quasisymmetric functions
item.description: arXiv:2610.21894v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We define a family of algebras $\mathbb{Q}[\mathbf{x}_n]/I_{n,a,b}$ whose Hilbert series, when $n\le a+b\le n+2$, $a>0$, and $0<b<n$, enumerate certain positroid cells by codimension. Equivalently, these series enumerate certain affine permutations by length. We determine the graded $\mathfrak{S}_n$-module structure of these algebras by using exact sequences to derive an invertible recursion for their graded Frobenius characteristics when $a+b\ge n$ and then passing to the limit $a\rightarrow\infty$. In particular, the graded Frobenius characteristic $\mathrm{grFrob}(\mathbb{Q}[\mathbf{x}_{a+b-1}]/I_{a+b-1,a,b};q)=\operatorname{rev}_q(\omega((\Theta_{e_{a-1}}\Theta_{e_{b-1}}\nabla e_1)\mid_{t=0}))$, where $\operatorname{rev}_q$ reverses the $q$-coefficients and the specialization $(\Theta_{e_{a-1}}\Theta_{e_{b-1}}\nabla e_1)\mid_{t=0}$ appears in the Theta conjecture. For $a,b\ge1$, we also show that $e_a^\perp\mathrm{grFrob}(\mathbb{Q}[\mathbf{x}_{a+b}]/I_{a+b,a,b};q)=q^{\binom{a}{2}}\operatorname{rev}_q(\omega((\Delta_{e_{a-1}}^\prime e_b)\mid_{t=0}))$, where $\Delta_{e_{k-1}}^\prime e_n$ occurs in the Delta conjecture. In the three cases $a+b-n=0,1,2$, the ungraded Frobenius characteristics agree with three families of Eulerian quasisymmetric functions, respectively. We also construct an open subvariety of $(\mathbb{P}^{k-1})^n$ whose rational Chow ring is isomorphic to $\mathbb{Q}[\mathbf{x}_n]/I_{n,k,n-k}$. This variety admits a stratification induced by certain positroids. Its strata need not be affine, and their codimension generating function equals $\mathrm{Hilb}(\mathbb{Q}[\mathbf{x}_n]/I_{n,k,n-k};q)$.
item.dc:creator: Hai Zhu

item.title: A variation on local trilinear form
item.description: arXiv:2610.21920v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $F$ be a $p$-adic field and $M$ the subgroup of $\mathrm{GL}_2^3(F)$ consisting of triples with equal determinants. For each unitary principal series $L$-packet of $M$ whose central character is trivial on the diagonal $F^\times$, we determine its unique member distinguished by the diagonal $\mathrm{GL}_2(F)$.
item.dc:creator: Yiyang Wang

item.title: On a conjecture of King-Tollu-Toumazet for rectangular Kostka coefficients
item.description: arXiv:2610.21921v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A conjecture of King, Tollu and Toumazet predicts the behavior of small Littlewood--Richardson coefficients under stretching: if $c^{\nu}_{\lambda,\mu}=3$, then $c^{M\nu}_{M\lambda,M\mu}$ equals $2M+1$ or $\binom{M+2}{2}$ for every positive integers $M$. This corresponds to the Hilbert functions of a conic, or of the projective plane. We prove their conjecture for all rectangular Kostka coefficients $K_{\lambda,\mathbf{a}}$. We realize them as the weight multiplicities of the homogeneous coordinate ring of the Grassmannian $\mathrm{Gr}(k,n)$, or equivalently the weight spaces of semi-invariants of the $n$-subspace quiver with dimension vector $\beta=(k,1,1,\dotsc,1)$. For a weight $\sigma$, we show that if $\beta$ is $\sigma$-stable, then the dimension of the corresponding weight space is at least $n-2$ when $k=2$ and at least $4$ for every Grassmannian other than $\mathrm{Gr}(2,4)$, $\mathrm{Gr}(2,5)$ and $\mathrm{Gr}(3,5)$. These three cases are precisely when the associated moduli space of $\sigma$-stable representations has dimension at most two. Via $\sigma$-stable decomposition, the two alternatives are determined as follows: $2M+1$ for $\mathrm{Gr}(2,4)$, and $\binom{M+2}{2}$ for $\mathrm{Gr}(2,5)$ and $\mathrm{Gr}(3,5)$.
item.dc:creator: Deepanshu Prasad

item.title: Multivariate $P$- and $Q$-polynomial structures of generalized Johnson association schemes
item.description: arXiv:2610.22058v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $\mathfrak X$ be a commutative association scheme of class $d$ on $X$. We construct the generalized Johnson association scheme $\mathfrak J_{n,h}(\mathfrak X)$ on partial maps from $[n]$ to $X$ with domains of size $h$. For $1\le h\le n-1$, we prove that $\mathfrak J_{n,h}(\mathfrak X)$ has $(d+1)$-variate $P$- and $Q$-polynomial structures. In particular, its multivariate $Q$-polynomial property answers affirmatively a problem posed for generalized Johnson association schemes arising from finite Gelfand pairs. We also determine the primitive idempotents and the two eigenmatrices, expressing the first eigenmatrix as a product of an Eberlein polynomial and a multivariate Krawtchouk polynomial, and the second eigenmatrix as a product of a Hahn polynomial and a multivariate Krawtchouk polynomial. For the multivariate factors, we use Mizukawa--Tanaka $(d+1,2d+2)$-hypergeometric functions. In an appendix, we identify the normalized columns of the second eigenmatrix with the known spherical functions in the finite Gelfand pair case. We also discuss the orthogonality relations and the imprimitivity arising from partial maps with the same domain, and explicitly describe the multivariate $P$- and $Q$-polynomial structures inherited by the blocks and the quotient.
item.dc:creator: Hirotake Kurihara

item.title: Gluing weak approximability along recollements
item.description: arXiv:2610.22161v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study whether weak approximability glues along recollements of triangulated categories that are compactly generated by a single object. This is applied to derived categories of complexes with quasi-coherent cohomology and prescribed support for quasi-compact quasi-separated algebraic spaces.
item.dc:creator: Pat Lank

item.title: Series of Fano quiver moduli from extended Dynkin quivers
item.description: arXiv:2610.22203v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Associated to small extended Dynkin quivers, we construct series of Fano varieties of fixed Picard rank at most five and arbitrary even dimension, which admit a very explicit description of their geometry. For example, they all admit a flat morphism to a projective space, whose general fiber is a product of projective lines. We also give a closed formula for all Betti numbers, and interpret this formula in terms of an action of a cohomological Hall algebra on the cohomology of all the varieties in a series.
item.dc:creator: Pieter Belmans, Markus Reineke

item.title: An infinite completely normal basis theorem
item.description: arXiv:2610.22247v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $L/K$ be an arbitrary Galois extension with group $G$, equipped with the Krull topology. Let $C(G,K)$ denote the $K$-vector space of continuous functions $G\to K$, with $K$ discrete and $G$ acting by left translation. We prove that there exists a $G$-equivariant $K$-linear isomorphism $\varphi:C(G,K)\to L$ such that, for every open subgroup $H$ of $G$, the map $\varphi^H:C(H,L^H)\to L$ induced by extension by zero and extension of scalars is an $H$-equivariant $L^H$-linear isomorphism. This gives a completely normal analogue of Lenstra's infinite normal basis theorem; the case of finite base fields was previously established in an equivalent form by Hachenberger.
item.dc:creator: Patrik Lundstr\"{o}m

item.title: Computing the center of a fusion category
item.description: arXiv:2406.13438v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present an algorithm for explicitly computing the categorical (Drinfeld) center of a pivotal fusion category. Our approach is based on decomposing the images of simple objects under the induction functor from the category to its center. We have implemented this algorithm in a general-purpose software framework TensorCategories for tensor categories that we develop within the open-source computer algebra system OSCAR. We compute explicit models for the centers in form of the tuples $(X,\gamma)$ where $X$ is an object and $\gamma$ is a half-braiding. From these models we can compute the $F$-symbols and $R$-symbols. Using the data from the AnyonWiki, we were able to compute the center together with its $F$-symbols and $R$-symbols for all the 279 multiplicity-free fusion categories up to rank 5, and furthermore some chosen examples of rank 6, including the Haagerup subfactor (presented in a separate paper). Some of these centers yield new high-rank and not multiplicity-free examples of modular categories, e.g. rank 21 and multiplicity 2.
item.dc:creator: Fabian M\"aurer, Ulrich Thiel

item.title: Higher Verlinde categories of reductive groups
item.description: arXiv:2601.11084v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We define tensor categories ${\sf Ver}_{p^n}(G)$ in characteristic $p$ for connected reductive groups $G$ and positive integers $n$, generalising the semisimple Verlinde categories ${\sf Ver}_p(G)$ originating from Gelfand-Kazhdan and the higher Verlinde categories ${\sf Ver}_{p^n}$ for ${\rm SL}_2$ defined by Benson-Etingof-Ostrik. The construction is based on the definition of ${\sf Ver}_{p^n}$ as an abelian envelope of a quotient of a category of tilting modules, but we also introduce an expanded construction which refines the ${\rm SL}_2$ case and gives new results. In particular, the union ${\sf Ver}_{p^\infty}(G)$ can be derived from the perfection of $G$; certain exact sequences in ${\sf Rep}G$ map to exact sequences in ${\sf Ver}_{p^n}(G)$; and the underlying abelian category of ${\sf Ver}_{p^n}$ can be expressed as a subcategory of ${\sf Rep}{\rm SL}_2$, or as a Serre quotient of a subcategory of ${\sf Rep}{\rm SL}_2$.
item.dc:creator: Joseph Newton

item.title: Inner Products and Banach Algebra structures on Bicomplex Numbers and Their Associated Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2607.06543v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we introduce various types of inner products and norms on the bicomplex number system $\mathbb{C}_2$, the bicomplex vector space ${\mathbb{C}_2}^{n}$, the space of bicomplex matrices ${C_2}^{m \times n}$, and the space of bicomplex polynomials $\mathbb{C}_2[\xi]_n$. We investigate the relationships among these inner products and norms, and establish several results. Furthermore, we prove that $\mathbb{C}_2$ and ${\mathbb{C}_2}^{n}$ are Banach algebras and Hilbert spaces. These results provide a unified framework for the study of inner product structures and normed linear spaces over bicomplex numbers and their associated spaces.
item.dc:creator: Prabhat Kumar, Fahed Zulfeqarr, Amit Ujlayan, Anjali Anjali, Akhil Prakash, M. Younus Bhat

item.title: On partial representations of pointed Hopf algebras
item.description: arXiv:2502.03642v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The theory of partial representations first appeared in the context of groups to deal with restrictions of representations to non-invariant subspaces. Partial representations of a group $G$ correspond to representations of a groupoid algebra constructed out of $G$. The notion of a partial representation can be extended to the context of Hopf algebras. For a Hopf algebra $H$, its partial representations correspond to representations of a Hopf algebroid $H_{par}$, also constructed out of data coming from $H$. In this work, we describe the structure of the algebra $H_{par}$ for $H$ being a pointed Hopf algebra with a finite group of grouplikes $G(H)$. This algebra can be explicitly written as a direct sum, reflecting the groupoid algebra associated to the group $G(H)$. Explicit examples of rank one Hopf algebras are done in the nilpotent and the non-nilpotent cases.
item.dc:creator: Arthur Rezende Alves Neto, Marcelo Muniz Alves, Eliezer Batista

item.title: A note on complex Lie Algebras isomorphic to their conjugate
item.description: arXiv:2604.06979v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A real Lie algebra defines by extension of scalars a complex Lie algebra that is isomorphic to its Galois conjugate. In this paper, we are interested in the converse property: given a complex Lie algebra that is isomorphic to its conjugate, is it defined over the real numbers? We prove the existence of a $10$-dimensional nilpotent complex Lie algebra for which the answer is negative, disproving a recent conjecture by Der\'e. In addition, we compute the generic obstruction to this descent problem in terms of Brauer groups.
item.dc:creator: Cyril Demarche

item.title: Inherent Trade-offs when Enforcing Correct Data Symmetries in Multi-head Self-attention
item.description: arXiv:2608.30417v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We give a complete characterization of equivariant multi-head self-attention (MHSA): if an MHSA layer is equivariant to a symmetry group $G$, then $G$ can only act by permuting head-clusters, with QK and OV matrices satisfying an equivariance constraint tied to the group action. As a consequence, we prove that any fixed MHSA architecture that achieves exact equivariance by polynomially parameterizing unconstrained MHSA parameters inevitably leads to expressivity loss within the class of equivariant maps: the equivariance locus of unconstrained MHSA forms a union of extremely many Zariski-irreducible components in a reduced parameter space, and any single architecture covers at most one. For $G=D_4$ acting on $C$ copies of the regular representation as the token feature space, we show that there are $\Omega(C^{64})$ components for eight attention heads. We illustrate this with experiments on artificial tasks and show that the predicted head-cluster structures can arise naturally when the attention layer is pressured to become equivariant.
item.dc:creator: T\=ikun \^Ong, Georg B\"okman

item.title: Robustness of quantum spectrum estimation: weak Schur sampling under noisy inputs
item.description: arXiv:2610.03582v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We initiate the study of weak Schur sampling (WSS) under noisy inputs. Many optimal quantum learning algorithms rely on this measurement, for instance in quantum spectrum estimation (QSE) and quantum state tomography (QST). The standard analysis of WSS, QSE and QST assumes that the $n$ input copies of the target state $\rho$ are identical, i.e. $\rho^{\otimes n}$. We study what happens when they are not, a more realistic noisy scenario that breaks the very permutation symmetry on which WSS is built. In the simplest model the input is a noisy product state: the copies are independent but not necessarily identical and each is $\epsilon$-close in trace distance to the $d$-dimensional target state $\rho$. A naive argument via the data-processing inequality allows the per-copy errors to accumulate to $n\epsilon$ on the measurement outcome. We show that for QSE via WSS this does not happen: the expected estimation error in total variation is at most $\epsilon+\eta(n,d)$, where $\eta(n,d)=O(d/\sqrt n)$ is the noiseless error, and the additive noise term $\epsilon$ is optimal. The output error does not grow with $n$ even though the input error does; in this sense WSS is robust. Beyond noisy product states, for arbitrary input $\omega$ we show that the error is at most $\eta(n,d)+\frac{1}{n}\|\omega-\rho^{\otimes n}\|_{W_1}$, where $W_1$ is the quantum Wasserstein distance of De Palma et al. In particular, our results imply, for the first time, noise-robustness of Keyl and Werner's seminal algorithm for QSE, more than two decades after its introduction. Finally, we show that the noise cannot be too bad: within our model of robustness the promise on the input cannot be weakened to closeness of single-copy marginals or to a global trace-distance budget alone, as in both cases some inputs defeat every measurement and estimator.
item.dc:creator: Vladyslav Visnevskyi, Laura Man\v{c}inska
